experiment.hypothesis: A permitted non-contact mapping traverse can reveal how skylight illumination and rough basaltic passages affect localization workflow continuity.
experiment.method: Proposed stationary LiDAR/photogrammetry and passive light logging under a park-approved protocol; no drilling or collecting assumed.
measurements_to_collect: Relative localization drift per metre traversed
Illuminance in lux with time and position
experiment.success_indicator: Predeclare allowable localization drift and repeated-map closure error for the particular instrument; no threshold here is an observed result or mission safety limit.
experiment.next_measurement: Park-approved georeferenced interior survey with quantified position uncertainty.

limitations: Named lava tube existence is documented; cave dimensions are agency descriptive values, not a new instrument survey.
No public surveyed entrance coordinate was verified in the consulted NPS sources; no entrance waypoint is supplied.
No radiation shielding, roof stability, vacuum compatibility or lunar cave geometry equivalence is established.
Research access, sampling, equipment and safety require actual land-manager review. Seasonal visitor information is not a current access guarantee.

coordinates.frame: Geographic latitude/longitude as published by USFS; geodetic datum not stated on page
coordinates.scope: Official Getting There recreation-site point; not a surveyed entrance

records.coordinate_scope: USFS publicly publishes a site point. Do not relabel it a precise entrance or replace it with a third-party point.
records.verified_feature: USFS documents a roughly mile-long lava tube formed from a Hart Prairie lava eruption.

measurements.method: Descriptive USFS seasonal range, not downloaded sensor data; instrument/epoch/uncertainty unavailable
measurements.spatial_scope: Named cave; interior sampling locations unspecified

measurements.method: USFS describes mile-long cave; approximate value with unknown survey basis

sources.title: USDA Forest Service — Lava River Cave
sources.locator: Getting There latitude/longitude; General Information; page updated2026-04-06

experiment.hypothesis: A permitted cave-air logging and non-contact navigation protocol can quantify terrestrial illumination/thermal workflow changes in a documented volcanic void.
experiment.method: Proposed repeated interior mapping plus calibrated air-temperature and light sensors; exact stations require permission and a verified entrance survey.
measurements_to_collect: Air temperature in degC at known times/depth positions
experiment.success_indicator: Report reproducibility and sensor uncertainty against predeclared instrument goals; no new experiment has occurred.
experiment.next_measurement: Obtain an approved georeferenced cave survey and sensor time series.

limitations: Published site coordinates are a recreation location; the entrance coordinate remains unassessed.
Reported Fahrenheit range is agency descriptive context, not measured uncertainty or a planetary thermal match.
Earth air circulation, atmosphere, biology and gravity differ from lunar/Martian subsurface conditions.
USFS current access/pass requirements must be rechecked before any fieldwork.

records.name: LCROSS Centaur impact site, Cabeus

coordinates.frame: Mean Earth selenocentric, Marshall et al.2012 Table1; no implicit frame transformation

uncertainty_m.source: Marshall et al.2012 Table1; abstract separately rounds115×44m

coordinates.scope: Post-impact Centaur localization, not Cabeus crater centre or another polar feature

records.verified_feature: Water ice/vapor detected spectroscopically in impact ejecta at one sampled permanently shadowed location.

measurements.method: LCROSS NIR absorption and UV/visible OH evidence, spectral retrieval plus estimated excavated sunlit regolith mass
measurements.spatial_scope: Excavated ejecta observable in the shepherding spacecraft instrument field of view; not crater-wide reserve

measurements.method: Maximum water vapor+ice within the instrument field of view reported in Colaprete et al.2010 abstract

uncertainty.level: Reported uncertainty; use source method for detailed interpretation

measurements.spatial_scope: Instrument field of view; not total crater deposit

sources.title: Colaprete et al.2010 — Detection of Water in the LCROSS Ejecta Plume
sources.locator: Science330,463–468; abstract and Table1; author-institution cached copy

sources.title: Marshall et al.2012 — Locating the LCROSS Impact Craters
sources.locator: Space Science Reviews167,71–92; Table1 on journal page73

sources.title: NASA SMD-LUN-102 RevA — Expected Volatile and Dust Hazards
sources.locator: Page15: LCROSS is one sampled Cabeus location; other regions require separate evidence

experiment.hypothesis: A controlled laboratory test using explicit ice-bearing simulant scenarios can evaluate volatile-preserving sampling procedures against known starting water fractions.
experiment.method: Use measured starting mass fractions in a controlled cold/vacuum facility; any5.6wt% mixture is an experimental scenario inspired by LCROSS, not a measured Earth-site value.
measurements_to_collect: Starting and recovered water mass in kg
Mass balance and recovery fraction with uncertainty
experiment.success_indicator: Predeclare an instrument-specific recovery/mass-balance requirement; no outcome is asserted.
experiment.next_measurement: Direct site-specific volatile composition, depth, heterogeneity and uncertainty at the actual mission target.

limitations: This is genuine LCROSS evidence at Cabeus, not a new measurement of any TerrainX polar feature.
The5.6wt% estimate cannot be transferred to Haworth, Shackleton, other candidate regions or any Earth site.
An ejecta-derived sampled abundance is not an extractable reserve, depth map or engineering guarantee.
Measured water evidence and Diviner modeled stability are distinct data classes.
Source coordinate frame is retained; precise raster association requires a validated frame transformation.
